Hi Alejandro / Sofia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call around API authentication and key management for the Redwood integration: 

Recap:
- Primary goals: secure machine-to-machine auth for server-side requests, automated key rotation to meet FintechCo's 90-day rotation policy, and scoped tokens for embeddings/rerankers.
- Integration touchpoints: SDK setup (node/python), routing to regional endpoints, structured outputs / tool-calling considerations, and embedding/reranker access patterns.

Recommendations (high-level):
1) Production: service accounts + short-lived JWTs (recommended) — issue from FintechCo IAM, exchange for short-lived tokens via our token endpoint; minimal operational overhead and aligns with compliance.
2) Alternative: API keys backed by KMS with automated rotation — simple to start, can be automated via our rotation webhook/KMS connector.
3) Scopes & least privilege: separate credentials for inference (generation/chat) vs embeddings/reranking; use token scopes to limit access surface.

Action items / next steps:
- SE workshop to walk SDK auth flows and sample code (Nikhil suggested availability Thu/ Fri next week)
- Deliver integration checklist and playbook (attached)
- Share proposed Mutual Action Plan (attached) and finalize timeline; target pilot in Q3.

Attachments: redwood-api-authn-playbook.pdf, integration-checklist.xlsx

Would you prefer an initial SE workshop with a focus on OAuth/JWT flow or a shorter session showing API key + rotation demo? I can loop Nikhil and Rishi on the technical call.

Hi Alejandro —

Great questions. Short answers up front, details below and we'll deep-dive in the SE workshop.

Summary:
- OAuth/JWT (service accounts + short-lived tokens): best for security & compliance (recommended). Accepts your existing IAM identities; tokens are short-lived and can be rotated without changing long-lived credentials. Slightly more infra work up-front, but minimal ongoing ops.
- API keys + automated rotation via AWS KMS: quicker to adopt; Redwood supports KMS-driven rotation and audit logging. If you need to start fast and iterate, this is a valid path to pilot.
- SDKs (node/python): both SDKs include token management helpers. For service-account flows we provide sample exchangers; for API keys the SDK will auto-retry on auth failure but you should surface rotation events from your KMS for a fully automated flow.

Technical notes:
- Scopes: we recommend issuing separate credentials for (a) inference/generation, (b) embeddings & reranking, and (c) admin/management actions. Tokens include a scope claim; runtime enforces scope-based access.
- Rotation & audit: Redwood's rotation connector can call your AWS KMS to rotate the key and write rotation events to our audit log (exportable via CloudWatch/Stackdriver/S3).
- Structured output & tool-calling: these are enforced at the token scope level; you can allow tool-calling only for particular service accounts.

Proposed mutual action plan (attached):
- Week 1: SE workshop (auth flows + SDK setup)
- Week 2: Integration sprint (sample auth exchange + rotate test)
- Week 3: Security review & sign-off

I'm proposing a 60-minute workshop on Thu 6/18 @10am PT with Nikhil (SE) and Rishi (CS) — does that work? If so, Nikhil will share a short tech agenda and pre-reads (I'll send the calendar invite).

I've attached a short MAM doc (proposed-mam.docx) as well.

Marissa

Thanks, scheduling looks good. Quick technical notes for the workshop agenda: 
- Token exchange: recommended pattern is service account key (long-lived, stored in KMS) -> exchange to short-lived JWT via your token broker -> call Redwood token endpoint (/v1/auth/exchange) to get scoped short-lived token (exp ~15m-1h).
- JWT claims: include iss (service account), aud (redwood-inference), scopes: [inference, embeddings] as needed.
- Rotation test: we'll demonstrate rotating the KMS-wrapped key and show a zero-downtime swap using the token broker approach.
- SDK samples: node/python snippets will be shared in the workshop folder.

I'll attach a small gist in the workshop invite with the sample header and curl commands. See you Thu 10am PT.
